parsed.why: Parent regime applies: national passport, facilities and custody exposures bind visitors. State protections (shield law, Most Protective tier, no restroom criminalisation beyond one trespass arrest) offset only partly; the documented trespass arrest and national custody harms keep it low-elevated, near parent average.

Parent national regime applies, but state shows no restroom or adult facility restriction, a documented trans-prisoner placement by identity, no hostile state policy aimed at adults, and a sports-policy capitulation. Dependent on national passport and entry rules, so modestly above parent.

Parent regime applies. State adds appointed-board pressure, youth-care draft rule, no statewide adult nondiscrimination coverage and no hate-crime enhancement, and document rules requiring surgery or provider letters; mostly thin-statute but regulatory-edge exposure, below parent average.

Parent regime applies to entry and custody, but the state adds strong public-accommodations nondiscrimination, hate-crime enhancement, self-determination of documents, shield law enforceable against out-of-state action and no facility exclusion; clearly above the national line.

Parent regime applies plus state-specific universal exposure: statewide facility exclusion by birth sex with a cause of action, no state nondiscrimination or hate-crime law, surgery-based marker change, and sports and youth-care bans. Documented near-Do-Not-Travel tier.
